plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 14.3.10
plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to evaluate the polar double integral of sin theta over the region R in the first quadrant outside the circle r = 2 and inside the cardioid r = 2(1 + cos theta). The figure shows both curves in polar coordinates: the circle r = 2 (blue) centered at the origin and the cardioid r = 2(1 + cos theta) (purple), which extends further to the right. The shaded region R (light blue) lies in the first quadrant between theta = 0 and theta = pi/2, bounded on the inside by the circle and on the outside by the cardioid; a red radial line at an intermediate angle shows a representative radial strip. The figure establishes the geometry of the integration region R needed to set up the polar iterated integral with inner limits from r = 2 to r = 2(1 + cos theta) and outer limits from theta = 0 to theta = pi/2.

interactionPlan.concept: A polar double integral's limits are read directly off the picture: the inner r-limits are the two bounding curves (here r=2 inside, r=f(θ) outside) and the outer θ-limits run from the region's starting ray to the angle where the two curves intersect.
elements: horizontal polar axis labeled θ = 0
vertical polar axis labeled θ = π/2
blue circle r = 2 centered at the origin, labeled 'r = 2'
purple cardioid r = 2(1 + cos θ), heart-shaped, extending right to r = 4 at θ = 0 and pinching at the origin on the left, labeled 'r = 2(1 + cos θ)'
light-blue shaded integration region R in the first quadrant, bounded inside by the circle and outside by the cardioid, between θ = 0 and θ = π/2
red radial strip line at an intermediate angle running from r = 2 out to the cardioid (representative inner-integration strip)
intersection point of the circle and cardioid on the vertical axis at (0, 2), i.e. θ = π/2

interactions.teaches: The outer radial limit of the inner integral is exactly the bounding curve's formula, and the upper θ-limit is the angle where that curve meets the inner circle r = 2 — editing the formula moves the purple curve, reshapes R, and shifts the intersection angle, so both limits visibly come from the geometry

interactions.label: θ (rad)
interactions.teaches: Sweeping θ moves the red radial strip and accumulates the swept sub-region from 0 up to the current angle, showing that the outer integral adds up these radial strips from θ = 0 to the intersection angle θ = π/2

demo_steps.title: Read the radial limits
demo_steps.narration: At any fixed angle the red strip runs from the inner circle r = 2 out to the cardioid r = 2(1 + cos θ); those two curves are the inner integral's lower and upper r-limits.

demo_steps.title: Sweep to accumulate the region
demo_steps.narration: Drag θ from 0 to π/2: the highlighted swept area grows until it fills all of R, and the sweep stops exactly where the cardioid meets the circle — that intersection angle is the outer integral's upper θ-limit.

demo_steps.title: Change the outer curve
demo_steps.narration: Edit the cardioid formula in the input box: the purple curve, the shaded region, and the intersection angle all update together, confirming that both the r-limits and the θ-limits are consequences of the boundary formulas, not fixed numbers.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: In polar coordinates the iterated integral's limits are the picture itself: inner limits are the two bounding radii at a fixed angle, and the outer θ-limits are the angles where the region begins and where the two bounding curves intersect.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Draw polar axes as a horizontal line (label θ = 0 to the right of origin) and a vertical line (label θ = π/2 above origin) crossing at the origin. Blue circle of radius 2 centered at origin. Purple cardioid r = 2(1+cos θ): maximum radius 4 along θ = 0 (right), passing through (0,2) at θ = π/2, pinching to the origin at θ = π (left lobe). Fill the first-quadrant region between the circle and cardioid in light blue (this full R is always visible). Overlay a slightly darker blue swept sub-region from θ = 0 to the current slider angle, with a red radial line at that angle from r = 2 to the cardioid. Curve and axis labels in italic serif math styling. When the cardioid formula is edited, recompute the first-quadrant intersection with r = 2 and clip the shaded region and θ-sweep to that angle.

discrepancies: The red representative ray in the source emanates from the origin out to the cardioid, but in the generated figure the red strip starts at the inner circle (r = 2) and only spans to the cardioid, so the ray's inner endpoint and overall length differ from the source.
The 'r = 2(1 + cos θ)' label is partially clipped/overlapped at the top edge — only '(1 + cos θ)' reads clearly while the 'r = 2' prefix is cut off behind the cardioid curve and the viewBox top.

A darker 'swept' sub-region overlay (θ = 0 to the slider angle) is drawn on top of the light-blue region; this interaction artifact has no counterpart in the static source and slightly muddies the single uniform shaded lens at the default step.

The shaded lens in the source is a single uniform light-blue fill between circle and cardioid over [0, π/2]; the generated default already shows a two-tone fill because the sweep slider sits at 0.79 rad rather than 0.
